sections.html:
Southington, nicknamed the Apple Valley, is a Hartford County town about 20 miles southwest of Hartford. It had 43,501 residents at the 2020 census, with 17,149 households and 18,154 housing units. Three villages, Plantsville, Marion and Milldale, each have their own post office and a feel of their own in the older housing around them. The town sits in a valley between ridges, and the Quinnipiac River crosses it.

A nine-member Town Council works with a town manager. Zoning, schools, finance, water and the town clerk each have separate elected bodies or offices, so a question about a deed goes to a different counter than a question about a zoning rule.

sections.h2: What the housing stock looks like
sections.html:
Southington began as a farming settlement and became a manufacturing center in the early 1900s. Once Interstate 84 was built in the mid 1960s it turned into a bedroom community. The count rose from 13,061 in 1950 to 30,946 in 1970 and passed 43,000 by 2010.

  • Colonial and nineteenth-century houses near the center and Plantsville, such as the Capt. Josiah Cowles House (c. 1750).
  • Capes and ranches from the 1950s and 1960s boom.
  • Later subdivisions across the valley floor and the lower slopes.

Dozens of Southington buildings are on the National Register of Historic Places, including the Marion, Plantsville and Southington Center historic districts. If you live in one, ask the town before you plan exterior changes.

The town sits at the foot of the Metacomet Ridge, with Ragged Mountain and Short Mountain on the eastern edge, so some lots slope hard. Retaining walls, runoff and long driveways are what buyers and appraisers study on a hillside parcel.

Low parcels along the Quinnipiac River and its brooks may sit near water. Ask your insurer for the flood zone status before you list. A powerful tornado hit the area on May 24, 1962, but wind and tree damage to roofs is the more usual trouble today, so look at yours.

Near the town center, the former Ideal Forging factory site is being prepared for a new redevelopment attempt, with soil cleanup funded by the EPA, the state and the town. If a buyer asks about former industrial land near your parcel, the town or the state environmental agency can answer for a specific address.

Waterbury connects to Metro-North rail. The Farmington Canal Greenway passes through Plantsville, and Lake Compounce and Mount Southington ski area are in town. If your house is close to the trail, the center or the highway ramps, put that in whatever you hand to a buyer.

Southington's biggest employers include the town itself, Hartford Healthcare and Webster Bank, and about 28 percent of workers are in manufacturing, mostly fabricated metals and aircraft parts. Plant closings and layoffs in those trades can leave a homeowner needing a quicker sale than a normal listing allows.

Sellers with an inherited house, a tax balance, a failed inspection or a move already on the calendar are the ones who most often choose cash. The offer gets compared against a listing after repairs, showing time, the conveyance tax and carrying costs come off, and if a listing wins for your house, that is a fine outcome.

The transfer itself is taxed. For a deed of $2,000 or more, the state takes 0.75 percent and the town takes 0.25 percent, a combined one percent on most homes (Section 12-494, Chapter 223). The state share rises on the high end of a residential price:

  • Up to $800,000: 0.75 percent state, 0.25 percent town.
  • From $800,000 to $2.5 million: 1.25 percent state on that slice.
  • Above $2.5 million: 2.25 percent state on that slice.
  • Exempt transfers include a principal residence given in lieu of foreclosure and a sale that does not cover the mortgages and priority tax liens.

The grantor files Form OP-236 when the deed is recorded. Southington's town code on the form is 131, and the town clerk can tell you whether myCTREC electronic filing is accepted.

sections.h2: Property tax dates and late interest
sections.html:
Each Connecticut town picks one, two or four installments, and the last has to be due at least 45 days before the fiscal year ends (Chapter 204). An installment not paid by the first day of the following month is delinquent, and interest runs at 18 percent a year with a $2 minimum unless the town waived it.

The Southington Tax Collector has the installment dates, the mill rate and any sewer charges. Get those before you pick a closing date, because the proration between you and the buyer is worked out from them. The Assessor can answer questions about the assessment itself.

An unpaid tax bill is common and rarely fatal to a sale. The balance and interest are normally paid from the proceeds at closing, so ask the tax collector for a written payoff figure and share it with your closing attorney early.

The attorney will search title for anything else attached to the house, such as a lien or an old mortgage not yet released, and will list every payoff on the closing statement. You will see your net before you sign.

sections.h2: Doing a cash sale without repairs
sections.html: We buy houses in Southington as-is, so you do not need to fix problems before you sell. The cost of repairs is part of how the offer is worked out. Gather the deed, mortgage statement and tax bill, bring photo ID and keys to the closing, and call or text us with the address when you want a number.

faqs.a: Yes. It is in the Capitol Planning Region, about 20 miles southwest of Hartford, and had 43,501 residents at the 2020 census.

faqs.q: What are the villages of Southington?
faqs.a: Plantsville, Marion and Milldale. Each has its own post office and its own older housing.

faqs.q: How much is the Connecticut conveyance tax on a Southington home?
faqs.a: On most homes it is one percent of the price, 0.75 percent to the state and 0.25 percent to the town. The state rate is higher on the part of a residential price above $800,000.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Southington house with an unpaid tax bill?
faqs.a: Usually. The balance and interest are typically paid from the proceeds at closing, so ask the tax collector for a payoff figure.

faqs.q: Do I need to fix problems before a cash sale?
faqs.a: No. We buy as-is, and repair costs are part of how we calculate the offer.
